children: Australia's balance on goods trade narrowed modestly in July as exports of gold eased after a very strong June, data showed on Thursday, while imports of fuel continued to decline.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported the balance on goods recorded a surplus of A$1.9 billion ($1.36 billion) in July, down from a revised A$2.3 billion in June. That was still above forecasts of a A$1.45 billion surplus.

Exports fell 3.3%, with non-monetary gold down 26% after a huge jump in June, while coal and iron ore also dipped. Overall imports fell 2.5%, led by a 12% drop in fuel, though imports of vehicles and data center equipment remained strong.
